newsitem.title: USA: Case Corp forms venture in Uzbekistan.
newsitem.headline: Case Corp forms venture in Uzbekistan.

text.p: Case Corp said Tuesday it will establish a production facility in Central Asia through a joint venture agreement signed today in Uzbekistan.
The facility will produce two-row cotton pickers for sale in Uzbekistan and surrounding countries.
Case will hold the majority share in the joint venture, UzCaseMash.

Other partners in the venture are Tashselmash, a local agricultural equipment manufacturer that makes cotton pickers, and Uzselkhozmash Holding, a state association for the manufacture of agricultural equipment.

"This is an important element in our continued development of business in Central Asia," Jean-Pierre Rosso, Case chairman, said in a statement. "It is one of several emerging markets in which we are establishing a strong presence that will provide significant future sales growth."

The facility will be located in the Uzbekistan capital of Tashkent. Initially, it will assemble 100 Case IH cotton pickers from modular kits shipped from Case's East Moline, Ill., facility, and will progressively increase the use of locally sourced components, Case said.
The units will be ready in time for the 1997 cotton harvest. The facility also will produce combine grain headers for use on Case IH combines as well as those produced by other companies.

"This joint venture will increase availability of our technologically advanced cotton pickers to Uzbekistan, already the world's fourth largest producer and second largest exporter of cotton, and further improve that country's productivity," Rosso added.

Last month, Case Credit, a wholly owned subsidiary of Case, formed a leasing company in Uzbekistan to secure foreign capital for financing of agricultural equipment purchases. Reuters Chicago Newsdesk - 312-408-8787
